Press a cell and notice which lights change. Each cell needs pressing at most once.
Pressing a cell flips it and its neighbours. Pressing the same cell twice cancels out, so each cell needs at most one press – order does not matter.

The computer won this time – but you can play again! Think about which move leaves your opponent a “losing” position.
There is no winning move from here – the computer would have to slip. Restart and watch where it went wrong.
Look for a move that leaves your opponent in a losing position. With two piles, try to make them equal.
With two piles just equalise them: take the difference from the bigger one. Then mirror your opponent on the other pile.
In the “last one loses” version play the same until only piles of size 1 remain – then leave your opponent an odd number of such piles.
